key_insight: A localized hybrid FEM–RFM solves elliptic interface problems by using random features only in interface-cut cells while keeping standard finite elements on the rest of the unfitted background mesh.
engineering_relevance: This reduces cost and modeling complexity for high-contrast, multi-interface, and irregular-domain problems where resolving the interface everywhere with full local enrichment would be expensive.
method: Split the Cartesian mesh into uncut FEM cells and a narrow interface band handled by local random-feature representations on both sides of the interface.
Enforce solution and flux jumps on the physical interface via residual equations, and couple FEM and RFM across an artificial grid-aligned interface using trace and normal-flux conditions.
Eliminate interior FEM unknowns by Schur reduction, then solve a reduced least-squares problem for coupling nodal values and random-feature coefficients.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical testing in 2D and 3D across high coefficient contrasts, nonsmooth and multiple interfaces, irregular outer boundaries, and a periodic bicontinuous composite homogenization problem.
watch_item: Performance may depend on stable coupling and conditioning in the narrow interface band, especially for highly irregular geometries or strong coefficient jumps.
paper_title: A Localized Hybrid Finite Element--Random Feature Method for Elliptic Interface Problems on Unfitted Meshes
